---
title: "Reliability Explorer"
---

How reliable is windowed accuracy as an individual-difference measure — and
how does that depend on the analysis window? This explorer computes
split-half reliability (children's trial sets split randomly in half,
half-means correlated across children, Spearman-Brown corrected) for a grid
of analysis windows, in your browser.

```{ojs rel-inputs}
viewof all_datasets = Inputs.toggle({ label: "All datasets", value: false })
viewof sel_datasets = Inputs.select(datasetNames, {
  label: "Datasets", multiple: 6, value: ["pomper_saffran_2016"],
  format: (d) => datasetLabel(d), disabled: all_datasets,
})
viewof age_range = interval([0, 84], {
  step: 1, value: [0, 84], label: "Ages (months)",
})
viewof my_window = interval([-1000, 4000], {
  step: 25, value: [300, 1800], label: "Your window (msec)",
})
viewof n_splits = Inputs.range([5, 50], {
  step: 5, value: 20, label: "Random splits",
})
viewof min_trials = Inputs.range([4, 20], {
  step: 1, value: 6, label: "Min trials per child",
})
viewof include_excluded = Inputs.toggle({ label: "Excluded trials", value: true })
```

The heatmap sweeps window **start** (−500 to 1500 ms) and **end** (1000 to
4000 ms); your window is marked ×.

```{ojs rel-lib}
//| output: false
// deterministic RNG so results are stable across reactive updates
function mulberry32(seed) {
  return function () {
    let t = (seed += 0x6d2b79f5);
    t = Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 15), t | 1);
    t ^= t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), t | 61);
    return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
  };
}

// per-trial prefix sums so any window's accuracy is O(1):
// samples run t0, t0+25, ...; cumTD[i]/cumT[i] = counts among samples < i
function trialPrefix(t0, runs) {
  let total = 0;
  for (const [, len] of runs) total += len;
  const cumTD = new Float64Array(total + 1);
  const cumT = new Float64Array(total + 1);
  let i = 0;
  for (const [aoi, len] of runs) {
    for (let k = 0; k < len; k++, i++) {
      cumTD[i + 1] = cumTD[i] + (aoi <= 1 ? 1 : 0);
      cumT[i + 1] = cumT[i] + (aoi === 0 ? 1 : 0);
    }
  }
  return { t0, total, cumTD, cumT };
}

function prefixAccuracy(p, wLo, wHi) {
  let lo = Math.ceil((wLo - p.t0) / STEP_MS);
  let hi = Math.floor((wHi - p.t0) / STEP_MS) + 1;
  lo = Math.max(0, lo);
  hi = Math.min(p.total, hi);
  if (hi <= lo) return null;
  const n = p.cumTD[hi] - p.cumTD[lo];
  if (n === 0) return null;
  return (p.cumT[hi] - p.cumT[lo]) / n;
}

function pearson(xs, ys) {
  const n = xs.length;
  const mx = d3.mean(xs);
  const my = d3.mean(ys);
  let sxy = 0;
  let sxx = 0;
  let syy = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    sxy += (xs[i] - mx) * (ys[i] - my);
    sxx += (xs[i] - mx) ** 2;
    syy += (ys[i] - my) ** 2;
  }
  return sxx > 0 && syy > 0 ? sxy / Math.sqrt(sxx * syy) : NaN;
}

// split-half (Spearman-Brown corrected), averaged over deterministic splits
function splitHalf(children, wLo, wHi, splits) {
  const usable = [];
  for (const trials of children) {
    const accs = [];
    for (const p of trials) {
      const a = prefixAccuracy(p, wLo, wHi);
      if (a != null) accs.push(a);
    }
    if (accs.length >= 2) usable.push(accs);
  }
  if (usable.length < 8) return { r: NaN, n: usable.length };
  const rs = [];
  for (let s = 0; s < splits; s++) {
    const rng = mulberry32(1234 + s);
    const h1 = [];
    const h2 = [];
    for (const accs of usable) {
      const idx = d3.shuffler(rng)(d3.range(accs.length));
      const half = Math.floor(accs.length / 2);
      h1.push(d3.mean(idx.slice(0, half), (i) => accs[i]));
      h2.push(d3.mean(idx.slice(half), (i) => accs[i]));
    }
    const r = pearson(h1, h2);
    if (!isNaN(r)) rs.push((2 * r) / (1 + r));
  }
  return { r: d3.mean(rs), n: usable.length };
}
```

```{ojs rel-data}
//| output: false
active_datasets = all_datasets ? datasetNames : sel_datasets
slices = Promise.all(active_datasets.map(loadSlice))

childTrials = {
  const rows = buildRows(slices, {
    ageLo: age_range[0], ageHi: age_range[1],
    includeExcluded: include_excluded, collapseWords: true,
  });
  const bySubj = d3.group(rows, (r) => `${r.dataset}|${r.aid}`);
  const out = [];
  for (const [, g] of bySubj) {
    if (g.length < min_trials) continue;
    out.push(g.map((r) => trialPrefix(r.t0, r.runs)));
  }
  return out;
}

windowGrid = {
  const starts = d3.range(-500, 1501, 250);
  const ends = d3.range(1000, 4001, 500);
  const cells = [];
  for (const s of starts) {
    for (const e of ends) {
      if (e - s < 500) continue;
      const { r, n } = splitHalf(childTrials, s, e, n_splits);
      cells.push({ start: s, end: e, r, n });
    }
  }
  return cells;
}

myR = splitHalf(childTrials, my_window[0], my_window[1], n_splits)
```

```{ojs rel-readout}
html`<p style="color:#374151; margin:0 0 0.5rem 0">
<b>Your window [${my_window[0]}, ${my_window[1]}] ms:</b>
split-half r = ${isNaN(myR.r) ? "— (too few children)" : myR.r.toFixed(2)}
across ${myR.n} children ·
best grid cell: ${(() => {
  const best = windowGrid.filter((d) => !isNaN(d.r))
    .sort((a, b) => b.r - a.r)[0];
  return best ? `[${best.start}, ${best.end}] ms (r = ${best.r.toFixed(2)})` : "—";
})()}</p>`
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Window heatmap

```{ojs rel-heatmap}
{
  document.querySelectorAll(".pb-spinner").forEach((el) => el.remove());
  return Plot.plot({
    width, height: 480,
    x: { label: "Window start (msec)", tickFormat: (d) => d },
    y: { label: "Window end (msec)", tickFormat: (d) => d },
    color: {
      legend: true, label: "Split-half r (corrected)", scheme: "viridis",
      domain: [Math.max(0, d3.min(windowGrid, (d) => d.r) ?? 0),
               d3.max(windowGrid, (d) => d.r) ?? 1],
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.cell(windowGrid.filter((d) => !isNaN(d.r)), {
        x: "start", y: "end", fill: "r",
        tip: true, title: (d) => `[${d.start}, ${d.end}] ms\nr = ${d.r.toFixed(2)}`,
      }),
      Plot.text([{ start: 250 * Math.round(my_window[0] / 250),
                   end: 500 * Math.round(my_window[1] / 500) }],
        { x: "start", y: "end", text: () => "×", fontSize: 22, fill: "#dc2626" }),
    ],
  });
}
```

Cells with too few children (< 8 usable) are blank. The × marks the grid
cell nearest your window.

### Reliability vs. window end

```{ojs rel-curve}
{
  const byStart = d3.group(windowGrid.filter((d) => !isNaN(d.r)), (d) => d.start);
  const data = Array.from(byStart, ([start, g]) => g.map((d) => ({ ...d }))).flat();
  return Plot.plot({
    width, height: 420, grid: true,
    x: { label: "Window end (msec)" },
    y: { label: "Split-half r (corrected)" },
    color: { legend: true, label: "Window start (msec)", scheme: "plasma" },
    marks: [
      Plot.lineY(data, { x: "end", y: "r", stroke: "start" }),
      Plot.dot(data, { x: "end", y: "r", fill: "start", r: 2.5 }),
    ],
  });
}
```
